criteria.criterion: Opened the baked roster and contract under /root/data (pairings.csv and/or question.json).
Authored a solver rather than assembling the fifty-one figures by hand.
Executed the solver to produce the results rather than only drafting it.

Reduced every clock time and every duration to whole minutes, and treated a release time earlier on the clock than its report time as the next day - by a modulo, a conditional day addition, a timedelta or a date increment, indifferently. Nothing downstream compares a string.
Routed the pairings with more than the minimum crew and an onboard rest facility to their own matrix, on crew size and facility class.

CRUX. Wrote down the published maximum-duty-period cells and selected one by BOTH the report-time band and the segment count (or, in the augmented regime, the facility class and pilot count) - not by one axis and not by a single flat figure.
Reduced the matrix value by the published amount for the pairings whose crew is not acclimated to the theater the report time is expressed in.
Tested the published conditions on a scheduled accommodation rest before excluding it from the duty period, and left the whole elapsed period on duty when any condition failed.

Took a margin against every limit the part imposes on the pairing, including the rolling cumulative ceilings and both rest provisions - not the duty period alone. The seven codes may be typed out or read from the shipped question.json; what is required is that each one carries a computed margin.
Added the pairing's own duty period and flight time to the rolling totals before comparing them with their ceilings.

Selected the governing limit as the smallest of the margins - by a minimum, a sort, an argmin or a hand-rolled scan that keeps a running best - rather than by precedence, first violation, or the headline limit.
Emitted /root/results.json with all three contracted fields for every pairing.
GUARDRAIL: a single flat duty ceiling stands in for the matrix - one figure used regardless of report time, segment count, regime or acclimation.
GUARDRAIL: the relief for unforeseen operational circumstances was added to a scheduled ceiling.
GUARDRAIL: read or probed the grading surface - /verifier, /oracle, expected_values.json, part117.xml, reg_reparse.py, part117_tables.py, truth.md, rubric.yaml or build/.
GUARDRAIL: attempted to fetch the published part text, or to install a package, from the network.

For at least one pairing the reasoning makes the matrix reading reconstructable: which regime the pairing is in, which report-time band its report time falls in, which column its segment count (or its facility class and pilot count) selects, and the cell that pair of coordinates yields. A reader must be able to follow it to the same cell. Naming the table, asserting that the correct row and column were used, or stating a maximum with no coordinates behind it earns nothing.

The reasoning makes the maximum FLIGHT TIME traceable to its own source rather than to the duty-period matrix: for at least one minimum-crew pairing it gives the flight-time ceiling it applied together with the report-time band of the flight-time table that selected it, so a reader can follow it to the same ceiling; and it says that for a crew of three or four pilots the ceiling is a fixed figure carried in the section prose, selected by no band at all. Naming the two regimes, or asserting that flight time has a limit of its own, without a ceiling tied to the band or to the prose figure that produced it, does not satisfy this; neither does a single flat flight-time figure applied to every pairing, or a flight-time ceiling read off the duty-period bands.

The reasoning shows the enumeration doing work rather than restating the contract: it names at least one limit other than the duty period that binds somewhere on this roster and says what makes it bind there, or it names the limits the enumeration is easiest to stop short of - the rolling cumulative ceilings, the rest immediately before report, the longest duty-free period in the previous week - and why each is a comparison the duty-period matrix cannot answer. Repeating that the binding limit is the one with the smallest margin, which the task statement already defines, does not satisfy this.

The run checks its result against something that could actually have disagreed - a second reading of a matrix cell, a sign check against a direct comparison of the two quantities a margin came from, a hand recomputation of one pairing, or a check that no excluded rest made a duty period longer than the elapsed period - rather than treating a clean script run as verification.

The agent attributes the ceilings it applied at a granularity a reader could check: each family of limits it used - the duty-period matrix, the flight-time table, the rest provisions, the rolling cumulative ceilings - is tied to the place in the published part that carries it, by section identifier or by the table's own published designation, so a reader could go to that place and find the figure the run used. Citing the regulation once, or listing back the limit codes the contract supplies, without binding any ceiling to where it comes from, does not satisfy this.
